text.p: European champions
Germany had little trouble brushing aside Armenia 5-1 in the
opening game of their World Cup campaign on Wednesday despite
missing seven key players.
Thomas Haessler scored from free kicks in the 20th and 39th
minute and skipper Juergen Klinsmann, out of form in the league,
scored his 41st international goal from a header in the 26th
minute.
With the Germans controlling the game at will, Fredi Bobic
scored in the 69th minute, within five minutes of replacing
Oliver Bierhoff, and Stefan Kuntz made it five with a free
header from the six-yard box in the 80th minute.
"We know we had play well to win. The team didn't
underestimate their opponents and concentrated well on their
game," German trainer Berti Vogts said of Germany's first match
in qualifying group nine.
But the Armenians almost shocked Vogts's side 16 minutes
from time when goalkeeper Andy Koepke could only parry a furious
free kick from Arutyun Vartanyan against the underside of the
bar, and defender Juergen Kohler had to clear the ensuing shot
off the line.
With the Germans visibly easing up, striker Karapet
Mikhaelyan stole in five minutes from time to chip the ball over
goalkeeper Andreas Koepke and give the Armenians a consolation
goal to delight the 50,000 home crowd.
There was an unusual twist after the break when Sarkis
Hovanesyan was substituted by the nephew of Armenian President
Levon Ter-Petrosyan. The match in the Armenian capital had
nearly been postponed two weeks ago due to civil unrest
following president Ter-Petrosyan re-election.
The game marked a successful international debut for
Borussia Moenchengladbach defender Stephan Passlack, who forced
his way in to Berti Vogts's squad with some strong performances
this season.
"Here in Armenia we could only have lost," said Germany's
captain Klinsmann, referring to the missing seven key players
including libero Matthias Sammer, midfield playmaker Andy
Moeller and defender Thomas Helmer.
"So our strategy was to play aggressively from the start
until we had one or two goals," Klinsmann said.
Teams:

Armenia - Roman Berezovsky, Michael Ter-Zakaryan, Sarkis Hovsepian, Yervand Sukiasyan, Vartan Khachaturyan, Sarkis Hovanesyan (Hakop Ter-Petrosyan, 46th minute), Arutyun Vartanyan (Vartan Minosyan 75th), Aramais Tonoyan (Arsen Avetisyan 46th), Hamlet Mkhitaryan, Karapet Mikaelyan, Erik Assaduryan

Germany - Andreas Koepke, Stephan Passlack, Stefan Reuter, Juergen Kohler, Markus Babbel, Dieter Eilts, Marco Bode (Stefan Kuntz 73rd minute), Mehmet Scholl, Thomas Haessler (Michael Tarnat 75th), Juergen Klinsmann, Oliver Bierhoff (Fredi Bobic 64th)
Referee: Pierluigi Collina (Italy)
